findings.title: Invalid ERB/Ruby code `end if` breaks template compilation
findings.body: Line 6 contains `<%- end if %>` which compiles to the Ruby statement `end if` with no preceding expression for the `if` modifier. This is a syntax error and will raise a SyntaxError at template-compile time whenever the `embed/best` view is actually rendered (both when posts are present and when they are not). The controller spec for this action mocks `TopicView.new` and doesn't render views, so this bug is not caught by the included tests. This should simply be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: NoMethodError when feed item has no content
findings.body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes `i.content` is always present. Many plain RSS 2.0 feeds only populate `<description>`, not `content:encoded`/Atom `<content>`, so `i.content` can be `nil`, raising `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil`. Since `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set on this scheduled job, such an exception will cause polling to silently fail (without retry) for any feed item lacking a content field, and potentially abort processing of all subsequent items in that run since the exception propagates out of the `each` loop.

findings.title: cook_method :raw_html bypasses sanitization entirely for imported content
findings.body: `cook` returns `raw` unmodified when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping the normal PrettyText rendering/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` (used both by `PollFeed` and by `TopicRetriever`/`import_remote`) creates posts with this cook_method, and the resulting `cooked` value is rendered unescaped via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `embed/best.html.erb` as well as in the normal topic view used throughout the rest of the application. Content coming from `PollFeed` (`TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`) is taken directly from the RSS/Atom feed with no tag allow-list (unlike `import_remote`, which at least constrains tags via Readability's `tags:`/`attributes:` options). A malicious or compromised feed can therefore inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript that is stored verbatim and rendered without sanitization to every visitor of the topic, constituting a stored XSS vector.

findings.title: Backwards/weak origin check for postMessage listener
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` checks whether `e.origin` is a substring of `discourseUrl`, rather than verifying that `e.origin` strictly equals (or is a prefix of) the Discourse origin. This is the wrong direction for an origin check: a message is accepted as long as `e.origin` happens to appear anywhere inside the `discourseUrl` string, which is a fragile comparison that can behave unexpectedly depending on how `discourseUrl` is configured (e.g. if it contains query params, paths, or other substrings). The check should compare the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` against `e.origin` with strict equality instead of using substring containment.

findings.title: Disqus import loses category assignment and original post timestamps
findings.body: The previous implementation created the first post with `category: category_id` (derived from the removed `--category`/`-c` option) and `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, preserving the thread's original category and creation date during import. The new call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` does not accept or forward either a category or a created_at value, so imported Disqus threads are now always created with no category and with the current time as their creation date instead of the original Disqus post date. This is both a feature removal (the `--category` CLI option still exists in `method_option` metadata removed from the diff but no longer has any effect) and a data-fidelity regression for anyone running this migration tool expecting historical dates/categories to be preserved.

findings.title: Unguarded race condition on `embed_url` uniqueness in TopicEmbed.import
findings.body: `self.import` does a plain `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` check and, if blank, proceeds to create a new Topic/Post and then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a `Topic.transaction` block. There is no locking (e.g. `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) around the blank-check, so two concurrent callers for the same `embed_url` (e.g. the hourly `PollFeed` job and a simultaneous `TopicRetriever`-triggered import from a visitor request) can both see `embed.blank? == true` and both attempt to create a topic/post and a `TopicEmbed` row. The unique index on `embed_url` (added in the accompanying migration) will cause the second `TopicEmbed.create!` to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, which is not rescued here, potentially leaving an orphaned Topic/Post with no corresponding `TopicEmbed` record if the surrounding nested transaction semantics don't fully roll back the already-created post (PostCreator#create uses its own internal `Post.transaction`).

findings.title: Full RSS feed re-poll triggered per unknown embed URL
findings.body: `perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, which downloads and parses the entire configured feed, every time a never-before-seen `embed_url` is requested and feed polling is enabled — even though the hourly scheduled `PollFeed` job already performs this work independently. The only throttle (`retrieved_recently?`) is keyed per `embed_url`, not per feed, so many distinct unseen embed URLs arriving in a short window (e.g. several different articles being embedded concurrently) can each trigger a full, redundant feed fetch/parse, which is wasteful and could amplify load against the external feed host.

findings.title: Controller spec never renders views, hiding template errors
findings.body: The success-path examples stub `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed`/`TopicView.new`/`TopicRetriever` and never actually render `embed/best.html.erb` or `embed/loading.html.erb` (the spec is not configured with `render_views: true`, and `TopicView.new` is merely expected to be called, not exercised). As a result, a real rendering error in the view (such as the invalid `<%- end if %>` in `best.html.erb`) is not caught by this test suite, even though this is the primary new user-facing code path added by the PR.
